extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and practitioners of journalism and news editors
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for selecting, producing, and evaluating news (news values, story suitability, sources, format/medium considerations, pressures, and professional norms) as discussed in a journalism/social-science textbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: news values (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined cluster of values that guide what becomes news (e.g., enduring values, ethnocentrism, individualism, leadership, moderatism, moral/social order, political, responsible capitalism, small-town pastoralism, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists multiple named news values and links them to story selection, objectivity, and journalists' judgments; see individual value entries for specific implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: enduring values
rubrics_metrics.description: Enduring values are defined journalistic values (listed separately in the text) that persistently shape news selection and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed as journalistic values and national values; related to professionalism and sources; influence objectivity and avoidance of pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: altruistic democracy (news value)
rubrics_metrics.description: News value oriented to promoting citizen participation and democratic ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among news values (with political and civic implications); influences selection of stories that support democratic engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: citizen participation (news value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Value that foregrounds stories supporting citizen involvement in public life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the political/enduring values cluster that affects what is deemed newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: class factors (news value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class-related considerations that affect news selection and representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects inclusion/exclusion of topics and reality judgments; linked to journalistic values and audience images.

rubrics_metrics.name: ethnocentrism (news value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency to prioritize stories that reflect the reporter's or audience's national/cultural perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a news value; affects foreign news, story framing, and inclusion/exclusion decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: individualism (news value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Value favoring personal, individual-centered stories and explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shapes prominence of people stories, hero narratives, and spotlighting individual actors in coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: leadership (leadership value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Value that assigns newsworthiness to leaders and leadership-tested events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Influences coverage of public officials and national ceremonies; contributes to which actors are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: moderatism (news value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for moderate perspectives and avoidance of extremist framings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears in news values and affects inclusion/exclusion and editorial balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: moral/social order (news value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Value prioritizing stories about social order, disorder, and morality (moral disorder news, social disorder news).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to select stories on protests, ghetto disturbances, crime, and social cohesion; tied to normative judgments about society.

rubrics_metrics.name: normality (news value)
rubrics_metrics.description: News preference for stories that reflect norms or deviations from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related to smallness/bigness and normality judgments affecting story inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: political (news value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Political orientation as a value that guides coverage of elections, officials, policy, and ideological balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Influences balance, fairness, and inclusion of political perspectives and polls; links to objectivity debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: responsible capitalism (news value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Value that gives newsworthiness to stories supporting or scrutinizing capitalist institutions responsibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects business/economic news and inclusion of corporate perspectives; listed among enduring values.

rubrics_metrics.name: smallness vs. bigness (news value)
rubrics_metrics.description: A value tension favoring small-scale stories (small-town pastoralism) or big, national stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shapes prominence of rural/suburban vs. national topics and story framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: small-town pastoralism (news value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nostalgic/value orientation that privileges small-town themes and perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among news values; informs audience images and story selection bias toward local/small-community angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Norm of detachment, balance, and impartial reporting used to guide journalistic practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linked to credibility, fairness, organizational reinforcement, response to pressure, and debates over value inclusion/exclusion; compensating mechanisms and limits discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: balance
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of presenting multiple perspectives to achieve perceived fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed in relation to objectivity, political coverage, and multiperspectival news; balance considerations inform story editing and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical criterion for equitable treatment of subjects and viewpoints in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears alongside objectivity and is tied to credibility and the FCC Fairness Doctrine historically.

rubrics_metrics.name: distortion (factual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factual distortion in reporting, including highlighting and exaggeration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed as harmful, with highlighting/exaggeration as forms; relates to journalistic methods and television tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: highlighting and exaggeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques that emphasize or overstate events/quotes to increase story impact; flagged as distortion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted harmful especially in TV news and by general/national reporters; antecedent to sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: journalistic methods / evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and methods (field work, participant observation, interviews, content analysis) used to gather and verify facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods affect credibility, reality judgments, and how distortion or accuracy are judged; journalistic evidence and facts discussed as requisites for news policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: importance considerations (story importance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgments about a story's impact, national interest factor, rank factor, and overall significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes impact, competition effect, variability, and relation to source considerations; guides prioritization and placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: novelty / freshness / novelty considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for new or novel material (fresh news) and novelty items in format and story selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to decide leads, covers, and to avoid 'stale' stories; tied to product considerations and audience appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: suitability and suitability considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Composite criterion for whether a story fits the medium/audience including action, clarity, completeness, freshness, pace, product, sources, and substantive fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined as a central criterion for story selection; see enumerated sub-elements (action, clarity, completeness, pace, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: suitability: action
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a story contains actionable or eventful elements appropriate for news treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of suitability; actionability increases newsworthiness and suitability for fronts/lead stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: suitability: clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The clarity and comprehensibility of a story for its intended audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical and clarity standards guide editing and story length decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: suitability: completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a story can be presented with sufficient completeness within production/space/time constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness affects placement and whether stories are postponed, shortened, or expanded.

rubrics_metrics.name: suitability: pace
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate rhythm and tempo (pace) for presentation of the story in its medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects TV lead structure and story length; listed among suitability/technical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: product considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial/product factors (format, novelty, quality, pacing, story mixture) that determine news product design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes format change, magazine vs. television differences, novelty, quality considerations, and audience boredom/interest management.

rubrics_metrics.name: quality considerations / technical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for story quality, including technical standards (e.g., clarity, craft, accuracy) and editorial quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in assessing story quality (story quality entries) and in production decisions (story length, photo selection).

rubrics_metrics.name: sources: reliability and trustworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of sources by articulateness, authoritativeness, availability, geographic/social proximity, and trustworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source considerations determine story suitability, reality judgments, and are central to source-management strategies; includes protecting sources and risks of paid sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: sources: availability and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical availability of sources and their ease of access for journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability is an 'availability factor' in story selection and can bias coverage toward accessible actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: sources: power and incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that sources possess power (ability to leak, withhold, stage events) and incentives that influence news content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source power influences story selection, press relations, and may create pressure or staged news/pseudo-events.

rubrics_metrics.name: investigative reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: In-depth reporting that exposes wrongdoing or otherwise reveals hidden facts; carries distinctive objectivity and credibility challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted alongside exposes and leaks; involves legal/ethical risks and high newsworthiness but also organizational and political pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: staging / pseudo-events
rubrics_metrics.description: Events staged by sources or journalists to create news (media events, staged documentaries), including restaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raises issues of authenticity and sourcing; affects how journalists evaluate newsworthiness and report context.

rubrics_metrics.name: self-censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists' anticipatory avoidance or suppression of material due to ideological, legal, or commercial fears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shown as defined, with extent discussed; linked to credibility, national security, paraideology, and pressures; includes unconscious forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: external pressure (advertisers, government, affiliates, interest groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial, political, and legal pressures on news organizations (advertisers, affiliates, government investigations, legal action, economic threats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described effects include chilling, avoidance, and influence on executives and story selection; responses and avoidance strategies discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: organizational considerations (news organizations and executives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bureaucratic and managerial structures, budgets, formal roles, and internal politics that shape news selection and production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes executive power, division of labor, morale, promotions, and how organizations reinforce objectivity or obstruct change.

rubrics_metrics.name: audience considerations and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience images, preferences, mail/feedback, demographic characteristics, and research that shape story selection, format, and product decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience research influences executives; audience as tool of government pressure noted; feedback channels (letters, mail) affect coverage choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: medium and format considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of medium (television, newsmagazine, newspaper) and format specifics (magazine back-of-book/front-of-book, TV anchors, specials) that determine story suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medium affects story length, pacing, picture selection, highlighting, and technical constraints; format change and technology are factors in story planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiperspectival news
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy/approach aiming to present multiple perspectives; considerations include balance, funding, feasibility, decentralization, and shared responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed as defined, described, and debated (democracy implications, feasibility, opposition); affects story selection and source inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: story production standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Production-level constraints and practices (deadlines, daily production rhythms, editing, highlight editing, ideological editing) that shape final stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes roles of beat reporters, camera crews, editors, norms about rehearing/rehearsing, and pressures arising from schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: photo/picture selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for choosing images (photo selection, color use) that complement or shape stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects covers and lead visuals in magazines and TV; tied to taste considerations and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: taste considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial judgments about decency, profanity/taboos, nudity, repetition taboo, sexual balance, and other cultural taste constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Influences self-censorship, story postponement, and editorial decisions; taste intersects with political and audience pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: story types and interest criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre/typology of news stories that carry intrinsic newsworthiness (human interest, gee‑whiz, man‑bites‑dog, people stories, hero stories, trend stories, service stories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as part of interest criteria and product mix; determines placement and format (e.g., features vs. leads).

rubrics_metrics.name: scoops, exclusives, and scoops value
rubrics_metrics.description: Value placed on exclusive information or scoops as high-priority news content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoop value affects competitive behavior, source cultivation, and editorial risk-taking.
